1a.question: Calculate the Income Elasticity of Demand (YED) when income changes from 27,000 to 27,195 and quantity changes from 140 to 144.
1a.extract: Context: Extract A details changing consumer demographics and rising average disposable incomes in regional test markets for a startup snack manufacturer.
1a.explanation: Calculated by % change in quantity demanded (2.86%) divided by % change in income (0.72%).

1b.question: Assess the importance of market segmentation for a small retail start-up launching a new product line.
1b.extract: Extract B: Boutique Apparel Co operates in a crowded clothing market dominated by fast-fashion giants. Managing Director Sarah plans to target vegan consumers aged 18-25 who prioritize ethical sourcing.
1b.correct_answer: Exemplar model covers targeting precise demographic/psychographic groups, minimizing waste on mass advertising, and capturing a profitable niche.
1b.explanation: Start-ups face liability of newness. Focusing on a distinct segment ensures higher marketing productivity and builds an initial loyal customer base.

2a.question: Evaluate the likely impact of a price increase on a business with high price elasticity of demand.
2a.extract: Extract C: CoffeeCorner operates in a saturated high street market where consumers can easily switch to automated vending or rival artisan cafés across the street.
2a.correct_answer: Exemplar model addresses disproportionate fall in demand leading to severe total revenue drop, unless offset by strong brand differentiation.
2a.explanation: When PED is elastic (>1), consumers are highly sensitive to price changes. Raising prices forces consumers to switch competitors instantly, destroying sales volume.
